coalitions.title: Without coalitions, B1 grows more even, not less
coalitions.caption: One dot per world (seeds 1 and 2), its median over iterations 500 to 1,000; the short bar is the middle of the two. Top: the Gini coefficient of the tokens (0 if every agent held the same, near 1 if one held all). Middle and bottom, on logarithmic axes: how many agents are born in an iteration, per hundred living, and how old the average agent is. "No coalitions": `allow_revolutions` off, so a node always goes to its largest staker. "Estates by wealth": the tokens of the dead shared out in proportion to what each survivor holds.
coalitions.recipe:
**Runs.** the pilot worlds of batch S ([Revolutions, handover and gifts](what-the-switches-did-in-pilots.md#revolutions-handover-and-gifts-the-switches-the-world-was-built-with)): B1 and B2 at 10,000 tokens, each with and without coalitions (`allow_revolutions` off), and B2 with the estates of the dead shared out by wealth (`redistribution` `by_tokens`), seeds 1 and 2, played to iteration 1,000

**Data.** From each pilot world's series, `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/S/<world>-s<seed>/series.jsonl`, one row an iteration after its game (`gini`, `births`, `nodes`, `meanAge`).

1. Keep each world's rows from iteration 500 to 1,000.
2. Births per hundred: 100 · births / agents, row by row. Take the median of each quantity.
3. One dot per world; the bar is the middle of a pair.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py wealthspread`.

rules.title: In round 3, the share-out of estates sets inequality; coalitions do not
rules.caption: Each dot is one of the 70 worlds of Experiment 40 that lived to the end of its run: the Gini coefficient of its tokens, averaged from iteration 100 to the end. The short bar is the median of a column. Top: the worlds by where their rule sends the tokens of agents that die. Middle: the same Gini coefficient over the Gini of the same tokens dealt out at random over the same agents (each holding at least one), so that a world of paupers, which cannot be very unequal, is not called even for that alone; on the dashed line a world is as unequal as chance would make it. Bottom: the worlds' Gini by how their game gives a node away: to the largest stake, with or without coalitions of smaller stakers that can outweigh it, or by a lottery weighted by the stakes (where coalitions are not drawn). Every other setting of each world was drawn at random too, so each column mixes many kinds of world.
rules.recipe:
**Runs.** the worlds of round 3 of the screen of random worlds that lived to the end of their 3,000 iterations (Experiment 40: 30,000 tokens, every setting drawn at random)

**Data.** From each world's averages over iterations 100 to the end, `research/screen/health.json` (from the screen's readings, `research/screen/measures.py`), and each run's own statistics, `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/stats.jsonl` (`redistributed`, `tokens`).

1. Read each living world's average Gini coefficient from `health.json` (`averages.gini`), and its Gini over a random deal's (`averages.gini_random`: each iteration's Gini over (m − 1)/(2m − 1), m the mean holding, the Gini of a random deal that leaves every agent at least one token).
2. Group the worlds by their drawn `redistribution`, and by `contest` and `allow_revolutions`.
3. One dot per world; the bar is the median.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py wealthspread`.

shared.title: Where more tokens pass from the dead to the living, worlds tend to be more even
shared.caption: Each dot is a world of Experiment 40 that lived, coloured by its share-out rule. Across, on a logarithmic axis: the share of all the world's tokens that a cleanup hands on from the dead to the living, averaged over every phase from iteration 100 to the end; it counts the estates of every agent that died, culled or starved (the starved hold nothing). Up: the world's Gini coefficient, averaged over the same stretch.
shared.recipe:
**Runs.** the worlds of round 3 of the screen of random worlds that lived to the end of their 3,000 iterations (Experiment 40: 30,000 tokens, every setting drawn at random)

**Data.** From each world's averages over iterations 100 to the end, `research/screen/health.json` (from the screen's readings, `research/screen/measures.py`), and each run's own statistics, `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/stats.jsonl` (`redistributed`, `tokens`).

1. For every phase from iteration 100 on: `redistributed` over `tokens` (the cleanup's handed-on tokens over all of them). Average over the phases.
2. Plot against the world's average Gini coefficient; colour by `redistribution`.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py wealthspread`.
